questions.question: In TCS NQT Numerical Ability: Two programmers, A and B, working together can complete a core banking module in 12 days. If A works alone for 8 days and B finishes the remaining work in 18 days, in how many days could A alone complete the entire module?
questions.explanation: Let daily work be a and b. a + b = 1/12. Work done: 8a + 18b = 1. Since 8a + 8b = 8/12 = 2/3, 10b = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3 => b = 1/30. Then a = 1/12 - 1/30 = (5-2)/60 = 3/60 = 1/20. Thus A alone takes 20 days.

questions.question: In a TCS campus placement exam, a train 240 meters long passes a railway platform 360 meters long in 30 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanation: Total distance = 240 + 360 = 600 meters. Speed = 600 / 30 = 20 m/s. In km/h = 20 * (18/5) = 72 km/h.

questions.question: A client invoice at TCS is paid with an 8% discount. If the client pays Rs. 44,160, what was the original invoice amount before the discount?
questions.explanation: Amount paid = 92% of original = 44,160. Original amount = 44,160 / 0.92 = Rs. 48,000.

questions.question: In TCS Reasoning Ability: Pointing to a photograph of a man, an IT analyst said, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the analyst related to the man in the photo?
questions.explanation: The speaker's mother's only daughter is the speaker herself (assuming female analyst). Therefore, she is the mother of the man in the photograph.

questions.question: Six software engineers (P, Q, R, S, T, U) are sitting around a circular conference table in TCS Siruseri. P is between S and T. Q is opposite P. U is to the immediate right of S. Who is sitting opposite T?
questions.explanation: Arranging around a 6-seat circle: P at 12 o'clock, Q at 6 o'clock. S and T are at 10 and 2 o'clock. U is to the right of S. By symmetry, the person opposite T is U.

questions.question: A software testing suite finds that the ratio of critical bugs to minor bugs is 3:7. If 28 minor bugs were logged, how many critical bugs were detected?
questions.explanation: Let multiplier be x. 7x = 28 => x = 4. Critical bugs = 3x = 3 * 4 = 12 critical bugs.

questions.question: Find the next number in the TCS NQT series: 7, 11, 19, 35, 67, ___?
questions.explanation: Differences: 11 - 7 = 4, 19 - 11 = 8, 35 - 19 = 16, 67 - 35 = 32. Differences double each step. Next difference = 64. Next number = 67 + 64 = 131.

questions.question: In how many different ways can the letters of the word 'CAMPUS' be arranged so that the vowels (A, U) always appear together?
questions.explanation: Bundle (A, U) as 1 item. Remaining consonants: C, M, P, S (4 letters). Total items = 4 + 1 = 5. They can be arranged in 5! = 120 ways. The vowels (A, U) can arrange internally in 2! = 2 ways. Total = 120 * 2 = 240 ways.

questions.question: A sum of money invested at compound interest in a TCS provident fund doubles itself in 5 years. In how many years will it become 8 times of itself at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Amount doubles (2^1) in 5 years. To become 8 times (2^3), time required = 3 * 5 = 15 years.

questions.question: In TCS Verbal Ability: Select the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'METICULOUS':
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise. The exact antonym is 'Careless'.

questions.question: Two dice are rolled simultaneously in a gaming project simulation. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers appearing on top is a prime number?
If 12 men or 18 women can harvest a contract in 14 days, in how many days can 8 men and 16 women finish the same contract?
questions.explanation: 12 Men = 18 Women => 1 Man = 1.5 Women. 8 Men = 12 Women. Total workforce = 12 + 16 = 28 Women. If 18 women take 14 days, 28 women take: (18 * 14) / 28 = 9 days.

questions.question: A person sells an IT certification voucher for Rs. 1,870 making a loss of 15%. At what price should it be sold to gain 15% profit?
questions.explanation: Cost Price * 0.85 = 1,870 => Cost Price = 1,870 / 0.85 = Rs. 2,200. Selling price for 15% gain = 2,200 * 1.15 = Rs. 2,530.

questions.question: In TCS Syllogisms: Statements: 1. All servers are computers. 2. Some computers are laptops. Conclusions: I. Some laptops are servers. II. No laptop is a server.
options: Either I or II follows (Complementary pair)
questions.correct_answer: Either I or II follows (Complementary pair)
questions.explanation: Laptops and servers have an indeterminate relationship. Since Conclusion I is 'Some' and Conclusion II is 'No' with identical subject and predicate, they form a complementary pair: Either I or II follows.

questions.question: A boat travels 24 km upstream in 6 hours and 36 km downstream in 4 hours. What is the speed of the river current?
questions.explanation: Upstream speed (u - v) = 24/6 = 4 km/h. Downstream speed (u + v) = 36/4 = 9 km/h. Current speed v = (9 - 4) / 2 = 5 / 2 = 2.5 km/h.

questions.question: Given two strings s1 and s2, write a function to check if s2 is a rotation of s1 using only one call to substring check.
questions.explanation: TCS classic: If lengths match, concatenate s1 + s1. If s2 is a rotation, it must exist as a substring within s1 + s1.

extra.title: String Rotation Check (TCS NQT)

questions.question: Given an integer array nums, find the contiguous subarray (containing at least one number) which has the largest sum and return its sum.
questions.explanation: Kadane's algorithm: Maintain current_sum = max(num, current_sum + num) and max_sum in a single O(N) pass.

extra.title: Maximum Subarray Sum (Kadane's Algorithm)

questions.question: Given an integer n, find the sum of all its unique prime factors. If n is prime, return n.
questions.explanation: Extract prime factors by checking 2, then odd numbers up to sqrt(N). Add unique factors to a set and compute their sum.

extra.title: Prime Factor Summation (TCS Coding Round 1)

questions.question: Given an array arr of positive integers, find all the leaders in the array. An element is a leader if it is strictly greater than all elements to its right. Return leaders in order of appearance.
questions.explanation: Scan from right to left while maintaining current_max. Any element > current_max is a leader. Reverse collected list at the end.

extra.title: Leaders in an Array (TCS Advanced Coding)

questions.question: Given an array of account transaction values and a target sum, determine whether there exists any pair of transactions whose sum equals target.
questions.explanation: Use a Hash Set to store seen numbers. For each x in arr, check if (target - x) is present in set.

extra.title: Pair Sum with Target in Core Banking Ledger

questions.question: Implement basic run-length encoding. For a string of consecutive repeating characters, compress it to character followed by its count.
questions.explanation: Traverse string counting consecutive identical characters, append char and count to StringBuilder upon character change.

extra.title: Word Frequency Compression (Run-Length)

questions.question: Given an N x N square matrix, write a function to check if the matrix is symmetric (equal to its transpose).
questions.explanation: Compare matrix[i][j] with matrix[j][i] for all i < j. If any mismatch occurs, return false.

extra.title: Matrix Transpose & Symmetry Check

questions.question: Given a large positive integer represented as a string, compute the difference between the sum of digits at odd positions and the sum of digits at even positions.
questions.explanation: Single pass loop over characters: if index % 2 == 0 add to even_sum, else odd_sum. Return absolute difference.

extra.title: Difference between Odd and Even Position Digits

questions.question: Explain the JVM Memory Model (Heap, Stack, Metaspace, Program Counter) and how Garbage Collection works during high-volume batch processing at TCS.
questions.explanation: The JVM divides memory into Stack (per-thread frames), Heap (Young Gen: Eden, S0, S1 and Old Gen), and Metaspace (class metadata). G1GC partitions heap into equal regions to clean garbage with predictable pause times.

questions.question: In enterprise core banking systems like TCS BaNCS, how does Spring Batch implement Chunk-Oriented Processing with ItemReader, ItemProcessor, and ItemWriter?
questions.explanation: Chunk processing reads data in chunks (e.g. 500 records), processes each item in memory, and writes the entire chunk within a single database transaction. This prevents OutOfMemory errors on multi-million row night settlement batches.

extra.company_focus: Tata Code of Conduct (TCOC), enterprise BFSI banking architecture, TCS BaNCS platform, Spring Batch processing, transaction integrity

questions.question: Explain the difference between First Level Cache and Second Level Cache in Hibernate ORM, and how caching minimizes database round-trips in high-traffic TCS client applications.
questions.explanation: First level cache is session-scoped (enabled by default). Second level cache is SessionFactory-scoped (shared across sessions) using providers like Ehcache or Redis to cache frequently read entities and query results.

questions.question: How do you resolve Database Deadlocks in Oracle / SQL Server when multiple batch threads concurrently update account balances in TCS financial software?
questions.explanation: Enforce a strict global lock acquisition ordering (e.g. always sort account IDs ascending before locking). Keep transactions short, use fine-grained row-level locks, and configure sensible deadlock detection timeouts.

questions.question: Explain the internal bucketing, segment locking, and CAS (Compare-And-Swap) mechanisms of Java ConcurrentHashMap compared to Collections.synchronizedMap.
questions.explanation: synchronizedMap locks the entire map on every operation. ConcurrentHashMap in Java 8 uses synchronized locks only on the individual bucket head node and CAS operations for node insertion, enabling multiple threads to read/write concurrently.

questions.question: How do you implement the Saga Pattern (Orchestration vs Choreography) to maintain data consistency across distributed microservices without 2PC (Two-Phase Commit)?
questions.explanation: Saga breaks distributed transactions into local transactions. Orchestrator coordinates each step and executes compensating transactions if a step fails. Choreography publishes events, and services react and compensate autonomously.

questions.question: Explain Database Normalization up to Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF). In what scenarios would a TCS architect intentionally denormalize tables in an analytical system?
questions.explanation: 1NF eliminates repeating groups; 2NF eliminates partial dependencies; 3NF eliminates transitive dependencies; BCNF ensures every determinant is a candidate key. Analytical data warehouses denormalize into Star schemas to avoid expensive multi-table joins.

questions.question: In Spring Boot applications, what is the difference between @Component, @Service, and @Repository annotations, and how does @Transactional handle rollback on exceptions?
questions.explanation: @Component is general-purpose; @Service denotes business logic; @Repository adds automatic exception translation to DataAccessException. @Transactional rolls back by default on RuntimeException and Error, but not checked exceptions.

questions.question: How does Apache Kafka ensure message ordering, and what happens when a consumer in a consumer group crashes during high-throughput transaction streaming?
questions.explanation: Kafka guarantees ordering strictly within a partition using partition keys. When a consumer crashes, a group rebalance reassigns partitions to surviving consumers based on stored consumer group offsets.

extra.company_focus: Tata Code of Conduct (TCOC), enterprise BFSI banking architecture, TCS BaNCS platform, Spring Batch processing, transaction integrity

questions.question: Explain the difference between RESTful API Idempotency and Safety. Which HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) are idempotent, and why is this critical in financial payment systems?
questions.explanation: Safe methods (GET, HEAD) do not modify server state. Idempotent methods (PUT, DELETE, GET) produce the same server state regardless of multiple identical executions. POST is neither safe nor idempotent.

questions.question: How do you tune database connection pools with HikariCP in TCS enterprise web applications to prevent connection leaks and starvation?
questions.explanation: Configure maximumPoolSize matching available database server CPU cores, set connectionTimeout to fail fast (e.g. 3000ms), and set leakDetectionThreshold (e.g. 2000ms) to log stack traces of unclosed connections.

extra.company_focus: Tata Code of Conduct (TCOC), enterprise BFSI banking architecture, TCS BaNCS platform, Spring Batch processing, transaction integrity

questions.question: Explain Java 17 modern features: Sealed Classes, Records, and Pattern Matching for switch, and how they simplify domain modeling in enterprise applications.
questions.explanation: Records eliminate boilerplate for immutable data carriers. Sealed classes restrict which other classes can extend them. Pattern matching for switch enables clean type checking without repetitive instanceof casts.

questions.question: What is the Circuit Breaker pattern with Resilience4j, and how does it protect downstream banking APIs from cascading microservice failures?
questions.explanation: Circuit Breaker monitors call failure rates. If failures exceed threshold (e.g. 50%), state changes from CLOSED to OPEN, immediately returning fallbacks without stressing failing downstream systems.

extra.company_focus: Tata Code of Conduct (TCOC), enterprise BFSI banking architecture, TCS BaNCS platform, Spring Batch processing, transaction integrity

questions.question: How does SQL B-Tree indexing speed up SELECT queries, and why does an index degrade performance on high-frequency INSERT and UPDATE operations?
questions.explanation: B-Tree index allows O(log N) search by traversing balanced tree nodes. However, every INSERT or UPDATE requires rebalancing tree nodes and splitting pages, creating disk write overhead.

questions.question: Explain the difference between Synchronous and Asynchronous execution using CompletableFuture in Java, and how custom ThreadPoolExecutors prevent thread exhaustion.
questions.explanation: CompletableFuture executes tasks asynchronously on a background thread pool without blocking the calling thread. Using custom thread pools separates mission-critical tasks from slow external I/O tasks.

questions.question: How can Generative AI and LLMs be utilized securely in TCS Core Banking (BFSI) applications without violating RBI / global financial data privacy regulations?
questions.explanation: Explain: On-premise air-gapped LLMs, automated PII masking before inference, strictly forbidding customer account numbers in prompt contexts, and audit logging.

questions.question: Describe how AI-assisted developer tools (GitHub Copilot) are integrated into TCS delivery centers to accelerate legacy COBOL/Java modernization while ensuring strict code quality.
questions.explanation: Discuss: Automated legacy code parsing, unit test generation with JUnit 5, human-in-the-loop validation, and static code quality gates in SonarQube.

questions.question: How do you implement an intelligent fraud detection scoring pipeline using machine learning models integrated with real-time Kafka transaction streams at TCS?
questions.explanation: Architecture: Kafka Streams pushes payment events to a lightweight inference model scoring risk probability in under 50ms; suspicious transactions trigger OTP challenges.

questions.question: How would you build an internal knowledge assistant for TCS employees to query complex client SLAs and compliance documents using RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)?
questions.explanation: Detail: Chunking PDF manuals, storing embeddings in an internal Milvus/PostgreSQL pgvector database, querying with open-source LLM, and generating responses with exact page citations.

questions.question: What strategies do you adopt to prevent AI hallucinations when generating technical architecture summary reports for enterprise TCS clients?
questions.explanation: Explain: Constraining generation to strictly retrieved context chunks, temperature=0.0, chain-of-thought verification, and human architect sign-off.

questions.question: How do you automate test case generation using Generative AI for legacy financial applications with zero existing unit test coverage?
questions.explanation: Explain: Feeding method signatures and business logic paths to LLM; generating parameterized tests covering edge cases (nulls, boundary values); executing in CI/CD sandbox.

questions.question: Describe how you monitor model drift in machine learning models deployed for client customer churn prediction in telecom or banking domains.
questions.explanation: Detail: Monitoring feature distribution shifts over time, tracking F1-score drop against monthly ground truth, and automated model retraining triggers.

questions.question: How do you ensure ethical AI and transparency when implementing algorithmic loan approval models at TCS for banking clients?
questions.explanation: Discuss: Eliminating protected demographic attributes, calculating disparate impact ratios, and generating clear human-readable explanation factors for loan rejection.

questions.question: How do you optimize LLM prompt engineering for complex legacy SQL query conversion to modern cloud data warehouses (Snowflake)?
questions.explanation: Explain: Few-shot prompting with paired legacy-to-modern SQL examples, DDL schema inclusion, and automated syntax validation using SQLGlot parser.

questions.question: How does TCS evaluate employee AI fluency and readiness to deploy AI-driven solutions across global client accounts?
questions.explanation: Discuss: Role-based AI fluency certifications, hands-on hackathons, prompt engineering labs, and responsible AI compliance training.

questions.question: Why do you specifically want to start your professional engineering journey at Tata Consultancy Services (TCS)?
questions.explanation: Highlight: Tata Group's legacy of trust and ethics, massive global project exposure, world-class continuous learning platforms, and career stability.

questions.question: The Tata Code of Conduct (TCOC) is central to TCS values. Describe a situation where you chose the ethically correct path despite pressure to take a shortcut.
questions.explanation: Demonstrate: High integrity, honesty in reporting project bugs or test results, and upholding ethical principles above convenience.

questions.question: TCS operates delivery centers across India (Siruseri, Hinjewadi, Gandhinagar, Kolkata) and client locations worldwide. Are you flexible with relocation and rotational shifts?
questions.explanation: Affirm: Eagerness to relocate, adaptability to client time zones, commitment to team goals, and openness to hybrid working policies.

questions.question: How do you handle working on a long-term enterprise maintenance project that requires learning an older or niche technology stack?
questions.explanation: Showcase: Positive learning attitude, recognizing the immense business value of enterprise core systems, and seeking opportunities to modernize.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you collaborated with a diverse team of peers on a college capstone or software project. How did you resolve differences?
questions.explanation: Use STAR: Focus on active listening, dividing responsibilities by individual strengths, and delivering a cohesive project on time.

questions.question: Describe a challenging deadline where your software code had multiple unexpected bugs right before release. How did you handle the pressure?
questions.explanation: Explain: Calm systematic debugging, prioritizing critical showstopper defects, transparent communication with the project lead, and working overtime.

questions.question: Where do you see yourself growing within TCS over the next 3 to 5 years as a software engineer?
questions.explanation: Connect: Aspiring to grow from Assistant System Engineer to Senior Developer/Tech Lead, earning cloud certifications, and mentoring juniors.

questions.question: How do you react when a client or technical lead requests major changes to a feature that you spent two weeks developing?
questions.explanation: Emphasize: Customer focus, understanding that business requirements evolve, asking clarifying questions, and pivoting without frustration.

questions.question: What differentiates you from other qualified candidates interviewing for TCS today?
questions.explanation: Combine: Strong algorithmic and computer science fundamentals, eagerness to learn enterprise architectures, and cultural alignment with Tata values.

questions.question: Do you have any questions for TCS regarding our project allocation, Initial Learning Program (ILP), or mentoring culture?
questions.explanation: Candidate should ask about ILP training, certifications support, or the transition from campus to corporate project delivery.

questions.question: In TCS NQT Numerical Ability: Two programmers, A and B, working together can complete a core banking module in 12 days. If A works alone for 8 days and B finishes the remaining work in 18 days, in how many days could A alone complete the entire module? [TCS Version]
questions.explanation: Let daily work be a and b. a + b = 1/12. Work done: 8a + 18b = 1. Since 8a + 8b = 8/12 = 2/3, 10b = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3 => b = 1/30. Then a = 1/12 - 1/30 = (5-2)/60 = 3/60 = 1/20. Thus A alone takes 20 days.

questions.question: In a TCS campus placement exam, a train 240 meters long passes a railway platform 360 meters long in 30 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h? [TCS Version]
questions.explanation: Total distance = 240 + 360 = 600 meters. Speed = 600 / 30 = 20 m/s. In km/h = 20 * (18/5) = 72 km/h.

questions.question: A client invoice at TCS is paid with an 8% discount. If the client pays Rs. 44,160, what was the original invoice amount before the discount? [TCS Version]
questions.explanation: Amount paid = 92% of original = 44,160. Original amount = 44,160 / 0.92 = Rs. 48,000.

questions.question: In TCS Reasoning Ability: Pointing to a photograph of a man, an IT analyst said, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the analyst related to the man in the photo? [TCS Version]
questions.explanation: The speaker's mother's only daughter is the speaker herself (assuming female analyst). Therefore, she is the mother of the man in the photograph.

questions.question: Six software engineers (P, Q, R, S, T, U) are sitting around a circular conference table in TCS Siruseri. P is between S and T. Q is opposite P. U is to the immediate right of S. Who is sitting opposite T? [TCS Version]
questions.explanation: Arranging around a 6-seat circle: P at 12 o'clock, Q at 6 o'clock. S and T are at 10 and 2 o'clock. U is to the right of S. By symmetry, the person opposite T is U.

questions.question: A software testing suite finds that the ratio of critical bugs to minor bugs is 3:7. If 28 minor bugs were logged, how many critical bugs were detected? [TCS Version]
questions.explanation: Let multiplier be x. 7x = 28 => x = 4. Critical bugs = 3x = 3 * 4 = 12 critical bugs.

questions.question: Find the next number in the TCS NQT series: 7, 11, 19, 35, 67, ___? [TCS Version]
questions.explanation: Differences: 11 - 7 = 4, 19 - 11 = 8, 35 - 19 = 16, 67 - 35 = 32. Differences double each step. Next difference = 64. Next number = 67 + 64 = 131.

questions.question: In how many different ways can the letters of the word 'CAMPUS' be arranged so that the vowels (A, U) always appear together? [TCS Version]
questions.explanation: Bundle (A, U) as 1 item. Remaining consonants: C, M, P, S (4 letters). Total items = 4 + 1 = 5. They can be arranged in 5! = 120 ways. The vowels (A, U) can arrange internally in 2! = 2 ways. Total = 120 * 2 = 240 ways.

questions.question: A sum of money invested at compound interest in a TCS provident fund doubles itself in 5 years. In how many years will it become 8 times of itself at the same rate? [TCS Version]
questions.explanation: Amount doubles (2^1) in 5 years. To become 8 times (2^3), time required = 3 * 5 = 15 years.

questions.question: In TCS Verbal Ability: Select the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to 'METICULOUS': [TCS Version]
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise. The exact antonym is 'Careless'.

questions.question: Two dice are rolled simultaneously in a gaming project simulation. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers appearing on top is a prime number? [TCS Version]
If 12 men or 18 women can harvest a contract in 14 days, in how many days can 8 men and 16 women finish the same contract? [TCS Version]
questions.explanation: 12 Men = 18 Women => 1 Man = 1.5 Women. 8 Men = 12 Women. Total workforce = 12 + 16 = 28 Women. If 18 women take 14 days, 28 women take: (18 * 14) / 28 = 9 days.

questions.question: A person sells an IT certification voucher for Rs. 1,870 making a loss of 15%. At what price should it be sold to gain 15% profit? [TCS Version]
questions.explanation: Cost Price * 0.85 = 1,870 => Cost Price = 1,870 / 0.85 = Rs. 2,200. Selling price for 15% gain = 2,200 * 1.15 = Rs. 2,530.

questions.question: In TCS Syllogisms: Statements: 1. All servers are computers. 2. Some computers are laptops. Conclusions: I. Some laptops are servers. II. No laptop is a server. [TCS Version]
options: Either I or II follows (Complementary pair)
questions.correct_answer: Either I or II follows (Complementary pair)
questions.explanation: Laptops and servers have an indeterminate relationship. Since Conclusion I is 'Some' and Conclusion II is 'No' with identical subject and predicate, they form a complementary pair: Either I or II follows.

questions.question: A boat travels 24 km upstream in 6 hours and 36 km downstream in 4 hours. What is the speed of the river current? [TCS Version]
questions.explanation: Upstream speed (u - v) = 24/6 = 4 km/h. Downstream speed (u + v) = 36/4 = 9 km/h. Current speed v = (9 - 4) / 2 = 5 / 2 = 2.5 km/h.

questions.question: How would you build an internal knowledge assistant for TCS employees to query complex client SLAs and compliance documents using RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)? [TCS AI Round]
questions.explanation: Detail: Chunking PDF manuals, storing embeddings in an internal Milvus/PostgreSQL pgvector database, querying with open-source LLM, and generating responses with exact page citations.

questions.question: What strategies do you adopt to prevent AI hallucinations when generating technical architecture summary reports for enterprise TCS clients? [TCS AI Round]
questions.explanation: Explain: Constraining generation to strictly retrieved context chunks, temperature=0.0, chain-of-thought verification, and human architect sign-off.

questions.question: How do you automate test case generation using Generative AI for legacy financial applications with zero existing unit test coverage? [TCS AI Round]
questions.explanation: Explain: Feeding method signatures and business logic paths to LLM; generating parameterized tests covering edge cases (nulls, boundary values); executing in CI/CD sandbox.

questions.question: Describe how you monitor model drift in machine learning models deployed for client customer churn prediction in telecom or banking domains. [TCS AI Round]
questions.explanation: Detail: Monitoring feature distribution shifts over time, tracking F1-score drop against monthly ground truth, and automated model retraining triggers.

questions.question: How do you ensure ethical AI and transparency when implementing algorithmic loan approval models at TCS for banking clients? [TCS AI Round]
questions.explanation: Discuss: Eliminating protected demographic attributes, calculating disparate impact ratios, and generating clear human-readable explanation factors for loan rejection.

questions.question: How do you optimize LLM prompt engineering for complex legacy SQL query conversion to modern cloud data warehouses (Snowflake)? [TCS AI Round]
questions.explanation: Explain: Few-shot prompting with paired legacy-to-modern SQL examples, DDL schema inclusion, and automated syntax validation using SQLGlot parser.

questions.question: How does TCS evaluate employee AI fluency and readiness to deploy AI-driven solutions across global client accounts? [TCS AI Round]
questions.explanation: Discuss: Role-based AI fluency certifications, hands-on hackathons, prompt engineering labs, and responsible AI compliance training.

questions.question: Why do you specifically want to start your professional engineering journey at Tata Consultancy Services (TCS)? [TCS Culture Dimension]
questions.explanation: Highlight: Tata Group's legacy of trust and ethics, massive global project exposure, world-class continuous learning platforms, and career stability.

questions.question: The Tata Code of Conduct (TCOC) is central to TCS values. Describe a situation where you chose the ethically correct path despite pressure to take a shortcut. [TCS Culture Dimension]
questions.explanation: Demonstrate: High integrity, honesty in reporting project bugs or test results, and upholding ethical principles above convenience.

questions.question: TCS operates delivery centers across India (Siruseri, Hinjewadi, Gandhinagar, Kolkata) and client locations worldwide. Are you flexible with relocation and rotational shifts? [TCS Culture Dimension]
questions.explanation: Affirm: Eagerness to relocate, adaptability to client time zones, commitment to team goals, and openness to hybrid working policies.

questions.question: How do you handle working on a long-term enterprise maintenance project that requires learning an older or niche technology stack? [TCS Culture Dimension]
questions.explanation: Showcase: Positive learning attitude, recognizing the immense business value of enterprise core systems, and seeking opportunities to modernize.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you collaborated with a diverse team of peers on a college capstone or software project. How did you resolve differences? [TCS Culture Dimension]
questions.explanation: Use STAR: Focus on active listening, dividing responsibilities by individual strengths, and delivering a cohesive project on time.

questions.question: Describe a challenging deadline where your software code had multiple unexpected bugs right before release. How did you handle the pressure? [TCS Culture Dimension]
questions.explanation: Explain: Calm systematic debugging, prioritizing critical showstopper defects, transparent communication with the project lead, and working overtime.

questions.question: Where do you see yourself growing within TCS over the next 3 to 5 years as a software engineer? [TCS Culture Dimension]
questions.explanation: Connect: Aspiring to grow from Assistant System Engineer to Senior Developer/Tech Lead, earning cloud certifications, and mentoring juniors.

questions.question: How do you react when a client or technical lead requests major changes to a feature that you spent two weeks developing? [TCS Culture Dimension]
questions.explanation: Emphasize: Customer focus, understanding that business requirements evolve, asking clarifying questions, and pivoting without frustration.

questions.question: What differentiates you from other qualified candidates interviewing for TCS today? [TCS Culture Dimension]
questions.explanation: Combine: Strong algorithmic and computer science fundamentals, eagerness to learn enterprise architectures, and cultural alignment with Tata values.

questions.question: Do you have any questions for TCS regarding our project allocation, Initial Learning Program (ILP), or mentoring culture? [TCS Culture Dimension]
questions.explanation: Candidate should ask about ILP training, certifications support, or the transition from campus to corporate project delivery.
